docs.task: How workspace MCP servers are configured, validated, and their tools offered to an execution.

asks: Explain how workspace MCP servers are configured.
Explain how that configuration is validated.
Explain how the servers' tools are offered to an execution.

data_flow.step: The user edits the MCP servers tab (or `workspace.toml`). The form maps `disabledTools` to `disabled_tools` and sends the whole `WorkspaceSettings`.

`POST /api/workspaces/{ws}/validate` and the PATCH save both call `WorkspaceRt::validate`, which runs `validate_settings` and so `ostra_core::config::validate_workspace`, which calls `mcp::validate`. Any issue blocks `save_settings`. `disabled_tools` entries are not checked (tool names are unknown without a connection).

`save_workspace` seals literal header/env values into the encrypted registry, writes `workspace.toml` (removing registry-only fields), and, if the file was already approved, records the new Rule A1 hash. The hash covers command, env, url, headers, oauth, name, and enabled only.
An execution is spawned. The native executor (or the harness `Wrapped::run`) calls `McpConnector::open(&spec)` with the `ExecutionSpec`, before any model call or harness start.

`Connector::open` returns early with no tools for a read-only inspect session; otherwise reads `workspace.toml` fresh, keeps enabled servers where `agents` is empty or contains the agent name, and calls `McpGateway::ready` for each concurrently.

`ready` reuses a live connection keyed by `(root, name)` and fingerprint, refetches `tools/list` when older than 30 seconds or after a `tools_changed` notice, honors a 20 second failure back-off, and otherwise connects from the approved copy of the file (Rule A1) and lists tools. An unreachable server yields a note, which the executor emits as one Status/Activity line.

For each listed tool: skip names in `disabled_tools`, compute the canonical name, deduplicate, and build an `ExecTool` with its `ToolDefinition` and `read_only`. The `ExecMcp` becomes `McpOpened.tools`.
Native: `inputs.read_only_mcp_tools` is set for the policy, the tools go into `ToolEnvConfig.mcp`, and `m.definitions()` is appended to the provider's tool list.

Harness: the same `McpTools` is stored in the execution's `ToolEnv`. The `ostra mcp-stdio` shim asks the bridge for its tool list; `ServerBridge::mcp_tools` returns Ostra's own tools followed by `definitions()` converted to bare names (`mcp::bare`). The harness lists them once at startup, as `mcp__ostra__<server>__<tool>`.

A call arrives. Native: `ostra_tools::execute` routes `is_gateway_tool` names to `mcp::run`. Harness: the hook passes it (Rule M2); `mcp_call` maps the bare name to canonical, runs `check` (Rule M1 plus permission rules, asking the user if needed), then `execute`. Both reach `ExecMcp::call`, which finds the tool in the fixed list (else `Unknown tool`), applies `timeout_secs`, restarts a dead client once, and calls `Client::call_tool` with the server-side name.

Separately, `GET /api/workspaces/{ws}/mcp` calls `McpGateway::status`, which connects every server in settings and returns `McpToolInfo` rows with `enabled = !cfg.disabled_tools.contains(&t.name)`. The UI renders these as switches.

patterns.description: `ostra_core::mcp::validate` pushes `ValidationIssue { path: "mcp_servers[i].field", message }` for each bad field and never fails fast. It is called from `validate_workspace` and so reaches both `POST /validate` and `save_settings`. Messages follow HANDOVER section 20: instruction first, then the reason. Per CLAUDE.md pattern 7, a bad value is a validation error at save, not a silent fallback at spawn.
patterns.name: Save-time validation by dotted path

patterns.description: `Connector::open` runs once per execution (native: `ostra-exec-native` run start; harness: `Wrapped::run` before the harness starts). It reads `workspace.toml` fresh, keeps servers where `mcp::serves(server, agent)`, connects each with `ready`, then for each listed tool skips `disabled_tools` entries (compared with the server-side tool name `t.name`), builds the canonical name via `mcp::canonical(mcp::bare_name(...))`, drops duplicate canonical names, and fills an empty description. The resulting `ExecMcp` is the single source for tool definitions, read-only names, and call dispatch, so a tool absent here is unknown to both executors (`ExecMcp::call` returns `Unknown tool`).
patterns.name: Per-execution tool set fixed at open

patterns.description: `ready` re-reads the approved workspace file and finds the server entry that equals the one asked for (`.find(|c| c == cfg)`, full `McpServerConfig` equality). A server entry that differs from the approved copy in any field, including `disabled_tools`, is therefore reported as pending approval at connect time even though `disabled_tools` is outside the approval hash; this is only reachable when the file on disk changed without going through Ostra's save (which re-records the hash).
patterns.name: Rule A1: connect only from the approved copy

patterns.description: Policy layer 2 allows any canonical gateway tool unless a permission rule decides, and in Plan mode only `read_only_mcp_tools` pass. Executors fill `read_only_mcp_tools` from `McpTools::read_only()`, so it contains only tools that survived `disabled_tools`.
patterns.name: Rule M1: configured means allowed, rules narrow

document.problem: Workspace servers are declared in `workspace.toml` as `[[mcp_servers]]` (`McpServerConfig`). Today the only per-tool control is `disabled_tools`, a denylist of server-side tool names: every tool a server lists is offered unless named there. The task asks how this configuration is validated at save time and how the surviving tools are collected and handed to an execution, native or harness, so that a change to tool selection (for example an allowlist) can be planned against the real code paths.

It does not cover OAuth internals, the HTTP/stdio transports, or the harness MCP stdio shim protocol beyond where it fetches the tool list. No external technology lookup was needed: the task touches only MCP behavior the repo already implements.

submit.findings_summary: Servers are `[[mcp_servers]]` entries (`McpServerConfig` in ostra-core/config.rs). `mcp::validate` checks them at save through `validate_workspace`: name, command or url, headers/oauth only on the right transport, agent names, and timeout. The Rule A1 approval hash covers only the command-bearing fields. `Connector::open` in ostra-server/src/mcp.rs builds each execution's fixed tool set. It keeps servers where `mcp::serves(server, agent)` is true, connects through `McpGateway::ready`, and drops tools named in `disabled_tools`. `disabled_tools` is the only per-tool filter. It matches the server-side tool name, is not validated at save, and is outside the approval hash. The native loop and the harness bridge (`ServerBridge::mcp_tools`/`mcp_call`) consume the same `ExecMcp`, so a filter in `open` covers both executors. Policy Rule M1 and Rule M2 govern how calls are allowed, and `server_status` plus the web `McpSection` toggle `disabled_tools`.

The harness-side `ostra mcp-stdio` shim protocol and per-harness adapter registration in ostra-exec-harness

docs.task: How tool calls pass the execution policy, and where an MCP tool call could be refused.

asks: Explain how tool calls pass the execution policy.
Identify where an MCP tool call could be refused.

data_flow.step: Native loop: the model emits a tool_use block. tool_end canonicalizes the call (`env.canonical_call`), emits ToolCall, rejects invalid JSON input, sets YOLO from the host, then calls `policy.check(&call)`.

check runs `layer1`. For a workspace MCP tool name, no guard branch applies: not Report, Document, manage, submit_, PowerShell/Cmd, a file-writing or reading tool, Grep/Glob, or Bash. The one layer 1 branch that fires on any tool is `answer_only`, and it lists only write paths, Report, Document, Memory, manage tools, and shell targets, so an MCP tool is not stopped by it. layer1 returns None.

check runs `layer2`. `perms::family` gives Family::Other for mcp__ names. `known` is false for a gateway name but `mcp` is true. `rule_decision` looks at deny, ask, allow rules plus session allows. No rule: plan mode without a readOnlyHint gives Deny(`mode:plan`); otherwise Allow with no rule. A matching deny rule gives Deny(permission, rule text); a matching ask rule gives Ask.
check applies YOLO: Ask becomes Allow(`yolo`). Denials stand.

tool_end handles the decision: Deny returns an error tool_result to the model; Ask calls `host.ask_permission`; Deny from the user returns 'The user denied this call'; AlwaysInWorkspace adds a session allow rule equal to the tool name.

On Allow, `ostra_tools::execute` dispatches. A name that satisfies `is_gateway_tool` goes to `mcp::run`, which returns 'Unknown tool' when the execution opened no MCP tools, or calls `McpTools::call`. `ExecMcp::call` finds the tool in the execution's fixed list by canonical name and returns 'Unknown tool `x`.' otherwise. This is the refusal for a tool of a server that does not serve this agent, a tool in `disabled_tools`, or a name the model made up, because policy allowed it by M1 but the list does not contain it.

Harness run, before the call: `Connector::open` builds the list (servers filtered by `mcp::serves`, `disabled_tools` dropped, duplicate canonical names skipped). `Wrapped::run` passes read-only names into PolicyInputs and into ToolEnv, so the harness policy knows the same list as the shim.

Harness run, the shim lists tools: `tools/list` returns the submit tool plus `ServerBridge::mcp_tools`, which exposes Ostra's own tools by capability and the gateway tools from `env.config().mcp.definitions()` under bare names (`github__search`). An inspect (read-only) session gets none.

Harness run, the PreToolUse hook: the adapter parses the payload into a canonical ToolCall (a name like `mcp__ostra__github__search` becomes `mcp__github__search`). `decide` calls `policy_check`, which returns Allow with no rule for a gateway tool (M2) and runs the real policy only for other tools. Anything the adapter cannot parse is `PreParse::Refuse` and is denied.

Harness run, `tools/call` on the shim: `call_tool` canonicalizes the bare name, calls `decide` (again Allow for gateway tools), then `mcp_call`. `mcp_call` maps the bare name to the canonical name (`is_gateway_bare`, else the MCP_TOOLS table, else 'unknown tool'), runs `self.check` (which denies everything in an inspect session, otherwise `ExecutionPolicy::check`), resolves an Ask through `resolve_ask`, runs `ostra_tools::execute`, then observes and logs. Deny returns `Denied by {layer} `{rule}`: {reason}` as a tool error.

Settings feed the policy: workspace `permissions.allow/ask/deny` and `permissions.mode` reach ExecContext and are parsed with `perms::parse_rule` in `ExecutionPolicy::new` (invalid rules are logged and skipped). At save time `validate_settings` runs `validate_rule`, which only checks the name prefix for mcp__ rules.

patterns.description: ExecutionPolicy::check runs layer1 (guards, not overridable) and returns its denial. Otherwise it runs layer2 and, when YOLO is on, converts Ask and mode:bypass Allow into Allow(`yolo`). Deny from a guard, a deny rule, or plan mode stands under YOLO.
patterns.name: Single check entry point: layer 1 then layer 2, YOLO turns ask into allow

patterns.description: A canonical gateway tool (mcp__<server>__<tool>) has Family::Other. rule_decision is consulted first (deny, then ask, then allow including session allows). With no matching rule: plan mode and not marked read-only gives the plan-mode deny; otherwise known-or-gateway gives Allow with no rule. Every other unknown name, including a harness's own `Other:mcp__...` tool, gets mode_default: ask in default and acceptEdits, deny in plan, allow in bypass.
patterns.name: Workspace MCP tool decision (Rule M1) in layer2 Family::Other

patterns.description: deny first, then ask, then allow (config allow plus session allow). The deny message is 'Do not <describe>: the permission rule `<raw>` refuses it. If the task needs it, say so in your report.' with RuleRef::permission(raw). A server-wide rule `mcp__github` matches every `mcp__github__*` tool through the prefix test in Rule::matches (not for a gateway-name rule, which must match exactly).
patterns.name: Rule precedence inside rule_decision

patterns.description: In a harness run a workspace tool appears to the harness as mcp__ostra__<server>__<tool>. The PreToolUse hook adapter canonicalizes it to mcp__<server>__<tool>; ServerBridge::policy_check returns Allow{rule: None} for it without calling the policy (unless the session is an inspect session). The shim then calls HarnessBridge::call_tool, whose decide() goes to policy_check again (Allow again), and finally ServerBridge::mcp_call runs self.check (the real ExecutionPolicy::check), resolves an Ask with the user, executes, observes, and logs.
patterns.name: Rule M2: harness hook passes gateway tools, the MCP handler does the real check

patterns.description: All three surfaces treat Deny as a tool error whose text names the layer and rule and Ask as a question to the host (ask_permission or resolve_ask). The native loop and mcp_call write 'Denied by {layer} `{rule}`: {reason}'. The hook path wraps the same through denial_text. AlwaysInWorkspace answers add allow_rule_suggestion(call) to the in-memory session_allow; for a gateway tool the suggestion is the full tool name.
patterns.name: Per-surface handling of a policy decision

document.problem: Every tool call, including calls to workspace MCP servers, is meant to pass ExecutionPolicy::check. For MCP tools the path differs between the native loop and the harness executors, and the policy itself allows a workspace MCP tool by default (Rule M1). The only configured restrictions today are permission rules (deny, ask, allow), plan mode, a per-server disabled_tools denylist applied when the tool list is built, and a per-server agents list. There is no allowlist of tools per server.
document.scope: Task: how tool calls pass the execution policy, and where an MCP tool call could be refused. Covers the native loop, the harness hook bridge and MCP shim, ExecutionPolicy layer 1 and layer 2 for workspace MCP tools, and the non-policy places that can refuse an MCP call. It does not cover MCP client transport or OAuth (ostra-mcp), the sandbox, or the web UI.
document.title: Tool-call policy path and where an MCP tool call can be refused

submit.findings_summary: ExecutionPolicy::check runs layer 1 guards (none of which inspect workspace MCP tools) and then layer 2, where an mcp__server__tool name falls in Family::Other and is allowed by default under Rule M1. It is refused only by a matching deny rule (ask rules prompt), by plan mode unless the server marks the tool readOnlyHint, or by an inspect session. In harness runs the hook passes gateway tools unchecked (Rule M2) and the real check happens in ServerBridge::mcp_call. Outside the policy, a tool that is in disabled_tools, belongs to a server that does not serve the agent, or is not in the execution's fixed list is refused with 'Unknown tool' in ExecMcp::call. There is no per-server allowlist today, because allow rules do not restrict anything for MCP tools; rule validation only checks the mcp__ prefix.
